Strenuous

STREN-yoo-us -- stress on the first syllable, STREN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Strenuous is difficult, tough, or exhausting; requiring great effort.

Shoveling the driveway after the blizzard proved more strenuous than an hour at the gym.

Worked Example

On moving day, two friends wrestle a sleeper sofa up four flights of stairs, resting on every landing, arms shaking by the second floor.

That climb is strenuous: it demands great physical effort and leaves the body exhausted. Strenuous marks the work itself -- the task that makes muscles burn and lungs heave.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

taxing: demanding real effort or energy

exhausting: draining one's strength completely

grueling: punishingly tiring and severe

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

effortless: requiring no effort at all

restful: giving rest and relaxation

Where it sits · how much it wears you down — taxing → strenuous → grueling

taxing vs. strenuous: Taxing is milder than strenuous -- a taxing afternoon drains some of your energy, while a strenuous one demands hard physical effort from start to finish.

grueling vs. strenuous: Grueling grinds on past strenuous: a strenuous hike works every muscle, while a grueling one punishes you mile after mile until simply finishing feels heroic.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — strenu-

root — strenu-: vigorous, active, energetic (Latin strenuus 'vigorous, active')

suffix — -uous

suffix — -uous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Strenuous uses the -uous variant of this unit's suffix family. Latin strenuus described a vigorous, energetic person, and English kept the idea while shifting the angle: something strenuous is 'full of vigor-demanding effort' -- a task that requires all the energy a strenuus Roman was praised for having.

Use the root in a new word: strenuously

Use the root in a new word: strenuously: The mayor strenuously denied that the bridge project was behind schedule.

Word Building

Word Choice

Strenuous covers hard physical work -- strenuous exercise, a strenuous climb -- but notice its second life with effort of will: to 'strenuously object' or 'strenuously deny' is to push back with all one's might. Doctors' orders to 'avoid strenuous activity' use the physical sense.
